text:
To all the jobseekers-

I know the market is tough.
I also had a difficult time looking for a new role.

Just don't give up.
Not everything is your fault.

You can just try your best.
Give it all in.

Be brave.
Face the hardship.
Hold on for a while.

I know the time is rough but in the end it'll be all worth it.

You are enough.
Don't stop doubting your skills and preparation.

Time is tough and so are you.

Every time I poured my heart into 5-6 rounds of interviews and faced rejection, it felt like a punch in the gut. The sleepless nights, the endless preparation, all for nothing.

But looking back, I realize it wasn’t *nothing*. It was the Universe’s way of saying, *'Not this one, something better is on the way.'*

Every single time, I’ve been shown why that rejection happened.

Doors I thought I wanted to walk through were shut, only to have the right ones swing open.

The kind that aligned with my growth, my values, and my happiness.

At first, it stung. It hurt deeply. But now, when things don’t go as planned, I don’t panic.

I don’t question my worth. I sit back, breathe, and trust. The Universe knows.

I know there's another plan waiting. Something bigger, better, and just for me.

To anyone feeling the weight of rejection: trust that the closed doors are protecting you from something you can’t see right now.

Your path is being cleared for something even more beautiful.

Sometimes, we forget that a company’s brand name doesn’t define someone’s talent. It’s easy to get caught up in the 'big company = big talent' mindset, but that's not always the case.

I’ve had the privilege of working with people from smaller companies (lesser known) who blow me away with their skills and dedication. They don’t need a fancy title or a famous brand behind them to prove their worth.

I've seen the other side too—people in top-tier companies feeling lost, overwhelmed, or stuck, even though the world sees them as 'successful.'

Let’s stop attaching someone’s value to the company they work for. Freshers especially need to hear this—skills are what matter, not the size of the company behind them.

At the end of the day, happiness and growth don’t come from a brand name, they come from doing what you love and constantly improving your craft.

sapne dekhna achi baat hai,

lekin job ka sapna dekh ke 'interested' likhna,

yeh toh achi baat nahi hai na?

LinkedIn scams be like: 'Congratulations, you've been selected for a role you didn’t even apply for!'

The catch? Pay Rs. 50,000 for the honor.

You didn’t get that job.
Didn’t clear that exam.
Didn’t get promoted.
Didn’t feel seen.

And you’re wondering -

'Is something wrong with me?'

No.
Nothing is wrong with you.

You’re just in a phase called becoming.

Not everything blooms in one season.

You’re not behind.
You’re not slow.
You’re just human.

Keep watering your effort.
Your time will come.

Why didn’t you just quit if it was so toxic?'

Let me tell you why:

Because rent is real.
Because savings aren’t infinite.
Because interviews take time.
Because self-doubt is loud.

We don’t always stay in bad jobs because we want to.
We stay because we feel stuck.

So if someone finally gathers the courage to leave - don’t say 'you should’ve done it sooner.'

Say 'I’m proud of you for choosing yourself.'

That decision isn’t easy. It’s brave.

No mail.
No warning.
Just removed from Slack.

That’s how some people find out they’ve been laid off.

Not even a thank you for 2 years of dedication.

Layoffs aren’t always the problem.
The way you treat people is.

Worked late nights.
Skipped vacations.
Gave my 100%.

And when the layoffs came…
I was just an ID number.

Lesson?
Never give your mental peace to a company that wouldn’t even blink before replacing you.

Work hard, yes.
But work for yourself first.

Applied to 200 jobs.
Got 10 interviews.
3 ghosted.
2 rejected after 5 rounds.
1 said I’m 'overqualified.'

And the rest?
Silence.

Job hunting today is not about talent.
It’s about algorithms, timing, and luck.

If you’re feeling hopeless - this is your reminder:
You are not the problem.

The system is broken. And it needs fixing.

Let’s build a world where applications get respect, not rejection letters written by AI.

wake up at 5 AM.
Read 3 books a week.
Build a side hustle.
Learn to code.

Now repeat after me:

I am not a machine.

Productivity guilt is killing us slowly.

You don’t have to do everything.
You don’t have to earn rest.

You’re allowed to just exist.
And that - is enough.

You didn’t get the job.
It doesn’t mean you’re not good enough.

You got laid off.
It doesn’t mean you were a burden.

You’re unemployed.
It doesn’t mean you’re failing.

Your job is a part of your life - not the proof of your value.

You’re not a title.
You’re a human being.

And the right opportunity will never need you to lose yourself first.

500+ people commented 'Interested.'

Not a single one got a reply.

Why?

Because that job post was fake.

On LinkedIn, people prey on jobseekers' desperation just for likes and reach.

If you're posting fake jobs for clout - you're part of the problem.

And to everyone commenting 'Interested' - your worth is more than a desperate comment.

Say it with me:
No more begging. No more scams. No more silence.
